statement: You are given an array nums of non-negative integers. Choose some of its elements, with the rule that no two chosen elements may sit next to each other in the array.
Return the largest possible sum of the chosen elements. Choosing nothing is allowed and gives 0.
This is the same task as robbing a row of houses where two neighbouring houses cannot both be robbed.

examples.explanation: Pick indices 0, 3 and 6: 2 + 9 + 8 = 19. No two of them are neighbours.
Pick indices 0, 3 and 5: 5 + 100 + 5 = 110. Taking 100 rules out both 10s beside it, and that is still the best trade.
Taking both 9s (positions 2 and 5) is allowed because they are not next to each other: 9 + 9 = 18. Any choice that includes the 2 can take at most one of the 9s.
